genes.summary: Tumor-suppressor gene. Certain founder pathogenic variants are documented at elevated frequency in some reference groups, including Ashkenazi Jewish.
Tumor-suppressor gene. Specific founder pathogenic variants are documented in some reference groups, including Ashkenazi Jewish.
Beta-hexosaminidase A. Recessive. Specific pathogenic variants are documented at elevated carrier frequency in some reference groups, including Ashkenazi Jewish.
Beta-globin. Recessive. Carrier frequency of the HbS variant is elevated in populations with historical malaria exposure, including West African.
Arylsulfatase A. Recessive. A directly array-typable SNP variant; shown here as an assayed locus for contrast.

conditions.rationale: Specific BRCA1/BRCA2 founder pathogenic variants (e.g. 185delAG, 6174delT) occur at higher frequency among people with Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry. There is no single BRCA1 mutation responsible for breast cancer.
not_measured: These founder variants are small indels that consumer SNP arrays do not reliably type; they are reported not_assayed, never negative.
Most other BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variants, large rearrangements, and copy-number variants are not detectable here.
conditions.screening_note: Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry overlapping these loci is a reason to consider targeted founder-panel or full BRCA testing — it does not establish that a variant is present. Absence here does NOT rule a variant out, because the array cannot type these indels.

conditions.rationale: Certain HEXA founder variants (e.g. 1278insTATC) show elevated carrier frequency in Ashkenazi Jewish populations. Carrier status requires confirmatory testing and reflects reproductive-risk counseling, not personal disease.
not_measured: The HEXA founder variant is an insertion not reliably typed by consumer SNP arrays.
Enzyme-activity testing (the clinical standard for carrier screening) is not represented by SNP genotypes.
conditions.screening_note: Consider targeted HEXA testing or enzyme assay where reproductive-risk counseling is relevant, especially given Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry at this locus.

conditions.rationale: The HBB HbS allele (rs334) occurs at elevated frequency in West African ancestry populations, reflecting historical malaria selection. This is population context, not a personal diagnosis.
not_measured: Hemoglobin electrophoresis and full HBB sequencing are the clinical standards and are not represented here.
conditions.screening_note: An observed single HbS copy is consistent with sickle cell TRAIT (a carrier state), not sickle cell disease. Consider confirmatory hemoglobin testing and, where relevant, partner screening and counseling.

conditions.rationale: ARSA pathogenic variants cause MLD. The curated variant here is a directly array-typable SNP, included to show a clean assayed-and-not-found result alongside the not-assayed indels.
not_measured: Most ARSA pathogenic variants and the pseudodeficiency allele are not represented by this single SNP.
conditions.screening_note: This specific curated SNP was assayed and the clinical allele was not observed. That covers only this position, not the whole gene.

scores.missing_data_method: mean-imputation of model SNPs per model spec (synthetic)
scores.limitations: Synthetic polygenic score for demonstration. NOT a validated clinical model. Polygenic susceptibility is separate from high-impact Mendelian variant interpretation. No percentile or absolute risk is reported because no validated comparison distribution or calibrated model is available. PGS accuracy is known to be lower in non-European ancestries, which is directly relevant for this admixed individual.
